sentences.text: Two species are known: the type species T. albertii named by Meyer and Plieninger in 1844, and T. crocodilinus named by Quenstedt in 1858.
Currently, Termatosaurus is viewed as a dubious archosaur.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Termatosaurus as Phytosauria.
The time range for Termatosaurus is the Rhaetian, from 205.7 to 201.4 million years ago.
Fossils are found in the Upper Triassic of France, England, Germany, and Switzerland.
There is a debate over classification, with Oskar Kuhn suggesting it is a plesiosaur while other sources classify it as a phytosaur.
